entertainment.title: The Killers’ Dave Keuning Says He Survived a Major Stroke: ‘By Some Miracle I Am Fine’
entertainment.summary: The guitarist says doctors gave him a 40% chance of survival — and that the first thing he checked after surgery was whether he could still play.
entertainment.body:
The Killers guitarist Dave Keuning has revealed he suffered a major stroke two weeks ago and went straight into surgery.

Keuning, 50, shared the news in an Instagram post on Thursday (Nov. 26), writing that a blood clot had cut off the blood supply to the right side of his brain. “Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery,” he wrote. “The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital.”

“By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side,” Keuning continued, adding that even then he didn’t realize he was having a stroke. Doctors gave him a 40% chance of survival and told him to expect lasting disabilities, he said, “but by some miracle I am fine.” Related Olivia Rodrigo Shares Second Holiday Song 'Miss This Christmas' on Amazon Music Fuerza Regida Announces 'Pisteando Con La Regida Vol. 4' After Partial Legal Victory Against Rancho Humilde Goo Goo Dolls Fans Slam NBC Over Thanksgiving Halftime Show Snub: 'Badly Handled' Explore Brandon Flowers Keuning The Killers See latest videos, charts and news

“And yes I can play guitar just as good as before,” he wrote. “It was the first thing I checked when I woke up from surgery.”

“I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before,” he added. “I am thankful for my wife, my son, my daughter, and all of my bandmates, who I feel closer to than ever.”

A founding member of the Las Vegas band, Keuning stepped back from touring with the Killers in 2017 and has stayed off the road since, though he returned to the studio for 2021’s Pressure Machine . He has also released two solo albums under the name Keuning: Prismism (2019) and A Mild Case of Everything (2021).

The Killers earned their first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 2017’s Wonderful Wonderful and have notched eight No. 1 albums on the Official U.K. Albums Chart, most recently with 2023’s Rebel Diamonds . Their 2004 debut, Hot Fuss , produced “Mr. Brightside,” which in 2021 became the first song to log 260 weeks on the U.K. singles chart.

Brandon Flowers released his third solo album, Thrasher , in August, and has said he expects the next Killers album to arrive in 2027.

entertainment.title: Jermaine Haley, WWE Wrestler Known as Bronson Reed, Dies at 38
entertainment.summary: Haley died Friday following medical complications, the WWE announced.
entertainment.body:
Jermaine Haley, the WWE wrestler known as Bronson Reed, has died. He was 38.

Haley died Friday following medical complications, the WWE announced. No further details were reported.

“Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE . But more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” the WWE shared in an Instagram post. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.” Related Stories Movies Gerald R. Molen, Oscar-Winning Producer on 'Schindler's List,' Dies at 91 Music Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65

Born in 1988 in Adelaide, South Australia, Haley began his professional wrestling career in 2007 under the names Jonah Rock and J-Rock in the Australian independent circuit. He accumulated titles and worked on various promotions before his transition into the WWE.

He officially joined the WWE in 2019, performing on its training ground NXT. He was would become an NXT North American champion, but was released in 2021. Haley continued competing with New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Impact Wrestling.

Haley did not stay away from the WWE for long, as he joined the main roster in 2022, and went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in 2024. His most recent WWE appearance was roughly three weeks ago at the Crown Jewel event in Saudi Arabia, where he faced off against Oba Femi.

Haley married his high school sweetheart, Paige, and they welcomed their first child in February 2024. As the WWE announced, his wife was pregnant with their second child at the time of his death.

The wrestling company announced that wrestler Bronson Reed (real name Jermaine Haley ) died on Nov. 27 at the age of 38, citing medical complications.

“Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE,” the company wrote in an Instagram tribute, “but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague.”

WWE also noted that Reed and his wife, Paige Haley , were expecting their second child together, adding, “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine's entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.”

No additional details about the medical complications that led to Reed’s death were shared.

The wrestler’s final WWE appearance came at Crown Jewel on Nov. 7, when he was thrown off the stage and through tables by Oba Femi during a tag team title match, according to Sports Illustrated . Reed reportedly suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney. He remained in a hospital in Saudi Arabia for treatment before returning home.

Born in Adelaide, Australia, Reed recalled that he’d always been interested in wrestling.

“I was always a fan of pro wrestling, since I can remember,” he shared with Sporting News in 2021. “I had my uncle who lived with us at the time, he was a huge wrestling fan, so as a little kid at 2, 3 years old, he was watching wrestling on TV and I guess I was sitting there watching as well. From there, I just became a fan."

"As a little kid, I was always like, ‘One day I’m going to be a wrestler,’ but you don’t know if that is going to happen,” he added. “As a teenager, I saw some local wrestling and that’s when I was like, maybe I can do this, join a school and learn how to do it locally."

Joseph Sohm/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover One of Tom Selleck's most popular television roles before "Blue Bloods" was as the titular private investigator on CBS' "Magnum, P.I." But it was not his first time playing a detective-for-hire. One of the most notorious detective shows of the 1970s was "The Rockford Files." As a detective show, it is often ranked with "Magnum, P.I." Tom Selleck even played another private eye on "The Rockford Files" before going on to play the mustachioed investigator on CBS' hit show.

The six-season drama aired on NBC from 1974 to 1980, featuring James Garner as the titular Los Angeles private investigator Jim Rockford. The series was well-acclaimed and won five Emmy awards, and a reboot is premiering on January 2, 2027 .

Lance White was a recurring character on "The Rockford Files," played fantastically by Selleck. He appeared in two episodes: Season 5's "White on White and Nearly Perfect," and Season 6's "Nice Guys Finish Dead." In contrast to the cynical and laid-back Jim, Lance is prim and proper, wearing fancy suits instead of a Hawaiian shirt. The role was written by producer Stephen J. Cannell, who previously cast Selleck in two television pilots that were never bought by a network. Cannell was a longtime friend of Selleck's, and even had a cameo as a hotel security supervisor in a Season 7 episode of "Magnum, P.I."

It wasn't until he spoke to James Garner, his fellow costar from "The Rockford Files," that he had a change of heart. When venting about his dislike for the script, Garner pointed out that if the studios specifically wanted him, he could use that as leverage to suggest character changes. Selleck took the advice and pushed for rewrites of the script that made his character more flawed and akin to Jim Rockford. Eventually, Magnum became the character we know today , and Selleck finally took the role.

entertainment.title: 5 NBC Dramas That Helped Define '80s Television
entertainment.summary: By the end of the 1980s, NBC had definitively planted its flag as one of the biggest names in television thanks to these dramas which defined the decade.
entertainment.body:
NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Shows like "Cheers" and "The Cosby Show" were some of NBC's most defining '80s sitcoms . The network began the decade lagging in its ratings, but by 1986 it dominated television, airing many of the most highly-rated shows of the time. These shows were part of historic shifts in television, but the change and success was not limited to sitcoms. During this iconic decade for television, NBC also aired some of its best dramas.

Led by network president Brandon Tartikoff from 1980 to 1991, NBC oversaw a complete shift in its dramatic programming. The genre welcomed excellent new aspects like serialized and realistic storytelling, larger casts, and bigger budgets. With wider character ensembles and overarching storylines, NBC aired some of the most groundbreaking and influential dramas of the decade.

Here is an unranked list of five of NBC's most defining dramas from the 1980s. While modern viewers may be accustomed to many of the aspects shared amongst the entries, audiences of the decade will never forget the change in television these shows signified.

The series focused on the officers of the Metropolitan Police Department's precinct on Hill Street, an urban area of an unnamed city. Led by Captain Frank Furillo (Daniel Travanti), the detectives and beat cops of the station navigated their tumultuous jobs while dealing with their own troubles.

By showcasing the cops' personal lives and shifting to serialized storytelling, "Hill Street Blues" paved the way for cop shows and television in general. Rather than fixed, idealistic portrayals of law enforcement, the 1980s ushered in a new era of gritty procedurals. It stands as one of the most iconic shows NBC aired during the decade, and also has one of the most recognizable opening theme songs.

The show centered on two detectives of the vice division of Miami's Metro-Dade Police Department. James Crockett (Don Johnson) and Ricardo Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas) are partnered detectives who routinely work undercover to unravel illegal operations like drug and arms trafficking. It was created by Michael Mann (who also created "Crime Story" , an unfairly forgotten cop drama from the same decade).

Unlike the urban ruggedness and semi-realistic portrayals of cops in "Hill Street Blues," "Miami Vice" was focused on entertainment and high-octane action. As such, it was one of the most expensive television projects of the 1980s. The licensing for the music alone amounted to around $10,000 per episode.

What a difference two years can make! The Season 2 finale of "The Hunting Wives," now streaming on Netflix, ends with a jaw-dropping time jump, revealing that Sophie and Margo's worst nightmares are still ahead of them. (And that's good news for the viewers, since we know the show has already been renewed for Season 3 .)

But first, a recap of the finale: Nadia's fatal car accident is the final straw for Callie, who reveals every single one of Margo's misdeeds to Sheriff Jonny. (Well, the ones she thinks she knows about, anyway.) Recognizing the love that Callie and Nadia shared, Jonny promises to get justice... but that promise is no match for Jed's offer to bring Jonny with him when he's elected Governor of Texas, so Jonny drops the issue, much to Callie's disapproval.

And Jonny isn't the only one who makes a deal with Jed. Margo, who initially intends to sink her husband's campaign and run away with Sophie, instead makes a different arrangement. She'll remain his dutiful wife as political career advances, and he'll once again make Callie and Sophie's legal troubles go away — as long they stay away from each other. But that's not good enough for Sophie, who also demands that Margo transfer $10 million into her bank account, or else she'll go public with Margo's recorded confession. "You cross this line, there's no coming back," Margo says, forgetting one thing: crossing the line is Sophie's favorite pastime.

The finale ends with Callie using a picture of Margo for target practice, Sophie anxiously waiting for the $10 million to land in her account, and Margo smiling alongside her husband on the campaign trail. Two years later, however, their stories are very different: an extremely well-dressed Sophie drops her black card at a swanky bar, where the news is reporting on Jed and Margo's latest push for anti-LGBTQ+ legislation. Sophie rightly acknowledges her ex-lover's hypocrisy, along with another choice word, before receiving a phone call from an unknown number. Surprise! It's Margo, breathing heavily... and covered in blood.

Netflix Even though we don't actually see the $10 million transfer into Sophie's account, showrunner Rebecca Perry Cutter confirms to TVLine that "the flash forward heavily implies that she got the money." "[Freeman] speaks from this low volcanic voice and anger and he comes back up with truth that is undeniable," the director explained, adding that he'd tell him, "Be angry, be angrier, now be dignified."

"The Civil War" was a critical and ratings success , becoming PBS' most-watched series in a decade. It also helped popularize what became known as the Ken Burns effect, a filmmaking technique that emphasizes panning across or zooming in or out on still images.

Years later, Freeman co-executive produced the limited series "The Gray House" alongside Kevin Costner. The historical Prime Video series tells the story of four women who spied for the Union during the American Civil War.

The Oscar winner explained in February 2026 that he is drawn to historical projects because much of history remains untold, and he feels a responsibility to shine a light on those stories.

"There's a nail and I want to hit it right on the head," he said on "The View" while discussing "The Gray House." "This country, we don't know our history because so much of it is buried. ... The time has come for us to break that barrier."

entertainment.body:
Comedy Central/YouTube Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It's been 20 years since "South Park" killed off Chef (Isaac Hayes), and fans still miss him. Chef was a much-needed voice of wisdom for the unruly young main characters throughout the first seven seasons.

Unfortunately, Isaac Hayes suffered from a serious stroke in January 2006, and in March 2006 he released a statement criticizing the show's depiction of Scientology, quitting the show in protest. It wouldn't be until a decade later that Hayes' son revealed the actor had never actually written that statement; someone in the Church of Scientology had taken advantage of Hayes' incapacitated state to put words in his mouth. Hayes' departure from "South Park" may have been a mess , but even before that revelation, fans still remembered his character fondly.

The good news is that if you're a "South Park" fan who wants to hear Chef's voice again, you can get that on the '70s drama "The Rockford Files." James Garner was the main star of that show, but Hayes played a memorable guest star in three separate episodes. He played Gandolph Finch, AKA Gandy, and was introduced in the 1976 episode "The Hammer of C Block" as a former prisoner hoping to find his dead girlfriend's real killer. It was an incredibly dark episode, and it'd be the first of three massively critically acclaimed episodes of the series starring Hayes.

NBC/Roku In February 1977, Hayes' second episode on the show ("Just Another Polish Wedding") aired. In this one, Hayes plays a new version of Gandy, who was now a private eye. He and Rockford once again become an investigative duo, and their chemistry was off the charts.

Hayes' final "Rockford Files" outing was "Second Chance," and it aired in October 1977. In this one, Hayes plays a dive bar bouncer who's dating a singer with a haunted past named Theda, played by Dionne Warwick. The episode helped promote the new album "A Man and a Woman," a collaboration of Hayes' and Warwick's.

James Garner, who played the titular Rockford, praised the series for its "great characters" and included Hayes' Gandy among the best of them. "Isaac, his character, he was a big, tough, mean guy in prison, but I [Rockford] befriended him," he told the TV Academy Foundation . Garner himself passed away in 2014 , but "The Rockford Files" is being rebooted on NBC with David Boreanaz as the new lead. Curious to see which actors have put the most time into the world of daytime soap operas ? Without further ado, these are the five longest-tenured actors in soaps who are still part of today's daytime television landscape.

Rogers is best known for her role as Maggie Horton, which she originated on "Days of Our Lives" in 1973 and for which she won a Daytime Emmy Award six years later in 1979. The character was introduced as a love interest for main character Mickey Horton (John Clarke), who had been part of the series since its premiere in 1965. The two characters ended up having a longtime marriage before Mickey's death in 2010. Maggie is still part of the series in the modern day and was married to Victor Kiriakis (John Aniston), founder of the massive in-world corporation Titan Industries, until his death in 2023.

It makes sense considering she has starred in over 3,000 episodes of "Days of Our Lives," which undoubtedly has kept Rogers quite busy. However, she made time for one-episode guest roles on "Love, American Style" in 1973, "Quincy, M.E." in 1977, "Little House on the Prairie" in 1980, and "Knight Rider" in 1985.

Hayes is perhaps best known for playing Julie Olson, the teen daughter of leads Addie Horton (Patricia Barry) and Ben Olson (Robert Knapp) and one of the original main characters when the show premiered in 1965. Prior to her soap career, Hayes did many one-episode guest appearances across television, including popular shows like "Lassie" and "Perry Mason." entertainment.title: Fuerza Regida Announces ‘Pisteando Con La Regida Vol. 4’ After Partial Legal Victory Against Rancho Humilde
entertainment.summary: “I’m free now they’ve finally taken their foot off the tiger’s neck,” frontman Jesús Ortiz Paz wrote in Spanish on Instagram.
entertainment.body:
Fuerza Regida is moving forward with new music following a partial legal victory in its ongoing dispute with regional Mexican label Rancho Humilde.

On Thursday (Nov. 26), the California-based música mexicana group, which graced Billboard ’s cover in October, announced that Pisteando Con La Regida Vol. 4 , the latest installment in its live album series, will arrive Dec. 3.

The project’s distribution partner has yet to be determined, with more details expected next week, a representative tells Billboard .

Fuerza Regida frontman Jesús Ortiz Paz revealed the album’s release date in an Instagram post featuring what appeared to be the project’s cover art. “I’m free now they’ve finally taken their foot off the tiger’s neck,” JOP wrote in Spanish alongside a photo gallery.

Fuerza Regida teased the project in October , when an Instagram post about 22 stolen live-performance videos included the hashtag #PisteandoConLaRegidaVol4, hinting at the title of the band’s upcoming album.

The PCLR Vol. 4 announcement comes one day after Fuerza Regida secured a legal victory against Rancho Humilde. On Wednesday (Nov. 25), a federal judge ruled that the label could no longer enforce its personal-services contract against the band’s four members beyond March 9, 2026, according to a ruling obtained by Billboard .

The dispute dates back to 2025, when Rancho Humilde sued the group over alleged breaches of its recording agreement. Fuerza Regida countersued , alleging the label had tried to “sabotage” its success. The group also claimed its deal with Rancho Humilde was void under California’s seven-year statute, which allows musicians to exit personal services contracts after that amount of time.

Judge Vera sided with Fuerza Regida on the seven-year statute question on Wednesday, though he noted in the decision that Rancho Humilde will be able to appeal. The rest of the lawsuit, including the claims for breach of contract, remains unresolved.

sports.title: Rams guard Bill Murray out for season after torn Achilles in first career start
sports.summary: A former undrafted rookie defensive lineman, Murray worked for years to reach the point where he could start on the offensive line.
sports.body:
Murray suffered a torn Achilles tendon in the game and will miss the rest of the season, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.

The 29-year-old Murray had a long and difficult road to reach the point where he was starting in the NFL. He originally signed with the Patriots as an undrafted free agent defensive tackle out of William & Mary and spent three seasons on the practice squad. The Patriots liked his athletic profile and work ethic, and when he couldn’t crack the gameday lineup on defense, they moved him to the offensive line, but after three years and only one game played, they released him.

Murray then signed with the Bears, got on the field as a backup offensive lineman for three games in two years in Chicago, and was released again.

In 2025, Murray returned to the Patriots’ practice squad, got cut, then signed with the Colts’ practice squad, and got cut again.

At the start of training camp this year Murray signed with the Rams, and after the Rams lost offensive linemen Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon to injuries last week, Murray finally got his chance to start this week.

That lasted three quarters, and now Murray’s season is over.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy admits he hasn't spent enough time with the defense
sports.summary: McCarthy vows to take a closer look at the situation in the offseason.
sports.body:
He was the same guy he always is, and he admitted that (as former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said this week), McCarthy hasn’t been sufficiently invested in the side of the ball that isn’t his personal expertise.

“I have not spent enough time with the defense ,” McCarthy told reporters. “You know, and that’s something that, as far as job responsibility, job description, you know, these are things that’ll be looked at in the offseason. But, you know, it’s a point in our year where we’re making adjustments and definitely conscientious of it. But at the end of the day, we have to all do our jobs and make sure we’re giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need that we can perform and play with that type of urgency, physicality that we played today.”

McCarthy prefaced his comments with a lesson he learned as a boy, growing up in Pittsburgh.

“My father used to tell me all the time as a kid, ‘You tell the truth, you only have to tell your story once,’” McCarthy said.

The truth is that this week has entailed two sharply different versions of reality, where both things can indeed be the truth. One, McCarthy (like all of us) has flaws. Two, Rodgers should not have spoken about them publicly.

Rodgers clumsily defended his decision to break the code of a football locker room by texting this to Al Michaels: “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.”

That’s fine, but how does disregarding the “sanctity” of the locker room (a word Rodgers undoubtedly selected in response to Tom Brady using it on Thursday ) create “accountability”? McCarthy is accountable to team owner Art Rooney II. Not to the media or the fans.

Also, who decides when breaking the code is justified in the name of “accountability” to people to whom McCarthy isn’t directly accountable? There’s no tribunal to whom Rodgers can apply for permission to disregard the privacy of a football team’s inner workings. He took it on himself.

sports.title: Mike Macdonald on Sam Darnold, when healthy: "I think he's done a good job"
sports.summary: Quarterback Sam Darnold is back as Seattle's starter this week, after missing two games due to quad and rib injuries.
sports.body:
On Friday, coach Mike Macdonald was asked to assess Darnold’s performance when healthy.

“I think he’s done a good job,” Macdonald said. “As a football team, we’ve been good enough to go 6-4, and we want to get better. Yeah, he’s right there with everybody else.”

Well, he’s not right there with the player who replaced him. Drew Lock has started three games and played all but one drive of another. His record is 4-0. Darnold is 2-4.

And their numbers are starkly different. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. Lock has thrown seven touchdown passes and no interceptions.

Lock’s games have come against the Patriots, the Cardinals twice, and the Raiders. Darnold has faced the Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, and Bears — a much tougher slate of opponents.

The Seahawks won a Super Bowl with Darnold. That counts for something. Still, they’re 6-4. They have an opportunity to get a seventh win on Sunday, with Brock Purdy out for the game against the 49ers.

sports.title: Carucci Take 2: No minimizing hurdle Bills cleared on path to top playoff seed
sports.summary: Beating the Chiefs will likely be the game to which we will point if (when?) the Bills finally make that elusive fifth Super Bowl appearance.

They could lose both games to the NFC opponents because of tiebreakers. Now, with the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs both losing this week, the Bills have a […]
sports.body: Last week, we told you that the Bills only needed to win their remaining AFC games and they would clinch the one seed in the AFC. They could lose both games to the NFC opponents because of tiebreakers. Now, with the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs both losing this week, the Bills have a new path to the one seed. sports.title: Burch has 130 yards rushing and a TD, Buffalo beats Arkon to clinch berth in MAC title game
sports.summary: Messiah Burch had 130 yards rushing and a touchdown on 24 carries, Jason Wright threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to Terrance Shelton Jr. and Buffalo beat Akron 17-9.

sports.title: No Aaron Rodgers? No problem. Steelers crush Broncos with dominant defense
sports.summary: Mason Rudolph did enough on a day when the Steelers' defense made life miserable for Bo Nix.
sports.body:
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix could do nothing in Pittsburgh, as the Steelers’ defense dominated in a 27-5 win.

Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph, starting for the first time since Aaron Rodgers was benched and released, played reasonably well, completing 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards, with one touchdown and no interceptions. The Steelers didn’t ask Rudolph to do a lot, but what they asked him to do, he did.

But the Steelers’ defense was outstanding. T.J. Watt recovered a Nix fumble in the end zone for one touchdown, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception for another touchdown, and the Steelers’ defense had a great day on a rainy Black Friday in Pittsburgh.

The win improves the Steelers’ record to 7-4 and erases any doubt that head coach Mike McCarthy can lead them to the playoffs this season. The loss drops the Broncos to 8-3, and raises questions about how far they can go with Nix at quarterback.

sports.title: Justin Herbert ruled out, DJ Uiagalelei to make first start vs. Patriots
sports.summary: It is officially going to be DJ Uiagalelei vs.
sports.body:
Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been ruled out with a concussion suffered during last week’s loss to the Jets.

Uiagalelei made his debut earlier this month against Houston, completing 2-of-7 passes for 24 yards with a touchdown.

Herbert has completed 62.4 percent of his passes for 1,851 yards with eight touchdowns and 11 interceptions so far this season.

Linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee) and running back Keaton Mitchell (knee) are also out.

Outside linebacker Akheem Mesidor (ankle) and receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) are doubtful.

Tight end David Njoku (shoulder), cornerback Tarheeb Still (ankle), defensive lineman Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) are questionable.

sports.title: 49ers announce Mac Jones will start vs. Seahawks, Brock Purdy is out
sports.summary: Purdy's ankle injury will force him to miss his first game of the season.
sports.body:
Brock Purdy, who is an MVP candidate this season, has not practiced all week with an ankle injury, and on Friday, head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that Purdy has been ruled out. Shanahan said Jones is ready to go and will play well on Sunday.

“Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac.”

Last year Jones started eight games while Purdy was hurt, and although Jones didn’t play as well as Purdy, he did play well enough for the 49ers to go 5-3 in those eight games.

Now the 49ers will hope Jones can play well enough to beat the defending Super Bowl champions in a game that has major implications for the NFC playoff race.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers: Sanctity of the locker room doesn't protect the coach from accountability
sports.summary: With Al Michaels calling today's game in Pittsburgh, ex-Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers texted Michaels to give his side of the nasty breakup he just had with the team and head coach Mike McCarthy.
sports.body:
During the fourth quarter of the Broncos-Steelers game, Michaels read a text from Rodgers, in which Rodgers claimed he in no way violated the sanctity of the Steelers’ locker room when he went on Pat McAfee’s show to detail his problems with McCarthy.

“A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room,” Rodgers said in the text Michaels read during the game. “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.”

Rodgers told McAfee that McCarthy, among other issues, wasn’t watching enough film, was sleeping in team meetings, and addressed the team as the “Packers” instead of the Steelers during halftime on Sunday.

McCarthy’s Steelers are dominating the Broncos today, which stands as a rebuke to Rodgers’ claim that McCarthy isn’t fit to be the team’s coach. But Rodgers was able to get his side of the story into the game, via his text to Michaels.

sports.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026: Updated AFC and NFC standings, bracket, tiebreakers for Week 12
sports.summary: The Steelers' dominant win over the Broncos showed they remain in the thick of the playoff race after the Aaron Rodgers fiasco.
sports.body:
1. Bills (10-1): Inside track for the No. 1 seed after beating the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

2. Broncos (8-3) : Currently ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West based on the better record in common games

3. Jaguars (7-3) : Loss to the Giants was a big blow to their hopes of earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

4. Bengals (7-3) : In control of the AFC North, but Monday night’s loss in Washington hurts.

5. Chiefs (8-3): Big loss to the Bills on Thanksgiving night.

6. Steelers (7-4) : Their Black Friday win over the Broncos answers any questions about the direction of this team after cutting Aaron Rodgers.

7. Browns (6-4) : Cleveland’s path to the playoffs is looking surprisingly easy.

8. Patriots (5-5) : Hard to see them competing without Drake Maye.

sports.title: Sam Darnold officially off injury report, set to start vs. 49ers
sports.summary: Sam Darnold is officially back.
sports.body:
As expected, the Seahawks’ quarterback is off the injury report and set to start against the 49ers on Sunday, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Friday afternoon.

Darnold has been listed as a full participant throughout the week after missing Seattle’s last two games with a quad injury. Darnold had also suffered a cracked rib in the Week 8 loss to the Bears.

Darnold has had turnover issues this season, throwing nine interceptions this season. He’s thrown at least one pick in each of his last six starts.

Seattle is 3-4 in games that Darnold has started and 3-0 in games with Lock as QB1. Lock also brought the Seahawks back in the Week 1 win over the Patriots after Darnold exited due to injury.

Additionally, the Seahawks have ruled out right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee), and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe) for Sunday’s game against the 49ers.

sports.title: Luke McCaffrey gives up No. 11 to Brandon Aiyuk
sports.summary: Receiver Brandon Aiyuk is back, and he'll be back in the only number he's ever worn in the NFL.
sports.body:
Via multiple reports, Aiyuk and Commanders receiver Luke McCaffrey have struck a deal to give No. 11 to Aiyuk, who joined the practice squad two days ago.

The move strongly suggests that Aiyuk will be making his debut for the Commanders, sooner rather than later. And, at a more subtle level, that he’s not being viewed by the organization as a guy who’s getting a last chance to show that he still has gas in the tank, but as a player that the Commanders regard as someone who will step in and contribute.

Aiyuk won’t play on Sunday at Arizona. He could be on the field as soon as Week 13, against the Titans.

sports.title: Brock Purdy not practicing on Friday, putting Mac Jones in line to start
sports.summary: It looks like 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy will not be able to play Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
sports.body:
Purdy is not practicing on Friday, according to multiple reporters on the scene. He has not been able to practice all week due to an ankle injury.

Jones has thrown only one pass this season in three appearances. Last year, he started eight games for San Francisco, going 5-3. In 11 total appearances for the club last year, he completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 2,151 yards with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

The 49ers’ full injury report with game statuses will be released later in the day.

sports.title: Browns sign LS Rex Sunahara to four-year extension
sports.summary: The Browns have signed a key special teams contributor to a new deal.
sports.body:
Cleveland announced on Friday that the club has signed long snapper Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.

Sunahara grew up in Northeast Ohio in Bay Village, which is around 18 miles from where the Browns play at Huntington Bank Field.

“It’s a dream come true. There’s no place I’d rather be,” Sunahara said, via Kelsey Russo of the team’s website. “There’s no team I’d rather be with, so it’s the best thing ever. It makes you really think about a lot of things, where the sacrifices that were made to help get me here, it makes you feel really good.”

Sunahara has appeared in 39 games for the Browns over the last three seasons, including all 17 last season and all 10 so far in 2026.

He and the rest of the Browns will play the Raiders on Sunday night this weekend.

sports.title: Bo Nix throws directly to Jalen Ramsey for pick-six as Steelers dominate the first half
sports.summary: The Broncos' offense has been awful today.
sports.body:
Nix threw a perfect pass directly to a wide-open Jalen Ramsey for a touchdown, which would be great if Ramsey played for the Broncos, but was not so great because Ramsey plays for the Steelers.

It’s impossible to tell what Nix thought he was doing on the play, but he threw the ball right into Ramsey’s hands, and Ramsey returned the interception 36 yards to the house for a pick-six that gave the Steelers a 24-5 lead.

It was the second Steelers defensive touchdown off a Nix turnover; Nix also dropped the ball in the first quarter and T.J. Watt recovered for a touchdown.

Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph hasn’t been great, but he’s been a lot better than Nix, and the Steelers are rolling over the Broncos in the first half.

sports.title: Brock Bowers questionable for Sunday night vs. Browns
sports.summary: The Raiders may get tight end Brock Bowers back for Sunday's game against the Browns.
sports.body:
Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters in his Friday press conference that Bowers is questionable for the contest.

Bowers is dealing with an ankle injury. While he was listed as limited on Wednesday and Thursday, he did not participate on Friday.

Bowers missed last week’s loss to the Broncos. If he does not play against the Browns, he’ll have some extended time to recover as the Raiders have a Week 13 bye.

The star tight end has 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns in eight games so far this season.

Kubiak also noted that offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson suffered a potentially significant injury during Friday’s practice and has been ruled out.

Defensive tackles Tonka Hemingway, Adam Butler, and Tim Keenan have all been ruled out for Sunday’s game as well.

Defensive tackle JJ Pegues and cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. are questionable.

sports.title: Alex Singleton tackles Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety as Steelers lead 14-5
sports.summary: The Broncos' offense can't do anything, but the defense has done something.
sports.body:
The latest big play on defense came via Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton, who tackled Steelers running back Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety. That made the score 14-2 Steelers. On the subsequent possession, the Broncos kicked a field goal to make it 14-5.

More bad news for the Steelers came when linebacker Jack Sawyer was ruled out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.

Pittsburgh has two touchdowns, one of which came from the defense when T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone. The Steelers’ other touchdown, a Mason Rudolph to DK Metcalf touchdown pass, was the game’s only offensive score.

Rudolph has been better than Nix so far, which few would have expected heading into the game. But this game has been less about the quarterbacks than about the defenses.

sports.title: Dan Quinn had an "absolutely fantastic experience" coaching with Mike McCarthy
sports.summary: With Wednesday's rant from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers painting a negative picture about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy that extended to his time with both the Packers and the Cowboys, those who have worked with him in those places will inevitably be asked about McCarthy.
sports.body:
Commanders coach Dan Quinn, who spent three years as McCarthy’s defensive coordinator in Dallas, got the question on Friday.

“I had a like absolutely fantastic experience coaching with Mike ,” Quinn said, via Ben Standig. “He’s part of the reason I wanted to go there. And over my three years with him, man, I learned a lot. So I can’t speak anything from Pittsburgh but what I can say is like, you know, like I had an unbelievable coaching experience with him. Like, detailed about it. Got me better, challenged me in a lot of ways with how I’m thinking, what it can be, so that would go into it.”

Some will say that Quinn is simply saying all the right things, and that he wouldn’t want to make McCarthy look bad by telling tales of irregularities that may have transpired behind closed doors.

sports.title: Mason Rudolph hits DK Metcalf for touchdown pass as Steelers take 14-0 lead over Broncos
sports.summary: It's been all Steelers in the first quarter in Pittsburgh.
sports.body:
Rudolph threw a well-placed pass toward Metcalf, who leapt into the air over Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain, reeled it in and landed in the end zone for a 22-yard touchdown.

It’s the first start of the season for Rudolph, who has replaced Aaron Rodgers as the Steelers’ quarterback. And it’s the first game for Metcalf since his ejection last week against the Eagles drew him a great deal of criticism — not just for his two personal foul penalties, but for the poor play he has exhibited all season.

There’s still plenty of time left, but in the first quarter, the Steelers look like they’re firing on all cylinders. They’re beating the Broncos 14-0.

sports.title: Tee Higgins did not practice Friday, questionable for Sunday vs. Saints
sports.summary: Bengals receiver Tee Higgins did not practice on Friday, but the injury should not keep him out of Sunday's game against the Saints.
sports.body:
Via Ben Baby of ESPN, head coach Zac Taylor told reporters after Friday’s practice that Higgins woke up with hamstring soreness and the team gave him a day to work through it.

In 10 games this season, Higgins has 867 receiving yards with seven touchdowns. He’s well on pace to set a career high in receiving yards in 2026.

Guard Dalton Risner (knees) is out. Returning from injured reserve, cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) is doubtful while receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is questionable.

sports.title: Joe Milton III praises the Eagles, possibly criticizes the Cowboys
sports.summary: Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III returned to Texas on Thursday and threw a significant wrench into the Cowboys' postseason plans (and, possibly, Philly's thinly-veiled soft tank).
sports.body:
“It was a lot going through my head from when I first got here in Dallas to when I left, all the time I spent doing scout team quarterback, all the times where I was trying to get in the game, when they were up in games, just trying to get more experience,” Milton said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “I mean, it was just great coming back here and playing in this stadium in Jerry’s World and seeing the guys that I worked hard with in fall camp and OTAs.”

He then focused on his current team. While possibly adding a little commentary regarding his former team.

“But I mean, it’s about the Eagles,” Milton said. “These guys show up every day. Nobody’s late to anything. Nobody’s complaining about anything. That’s all you can ask for. That’s the most important thing that I love about this team. I just know they’re going to keep fighting.”

The obvious implication is that, in Dallas, some guys were not showing up every day. Some guys were late. Some guys were complaining.

There are surely complaints today, one day after the Cowboys lost their fourth game of the season while scoring 30 or more points.

sports.title: Steelers score first as T.J. Watt recovers Bo Nix fumble in end zone
sports.summary: There hasn't been any offense on display in Pittsburgh so far on Black Friday, but there has been a touchdown.
sports.body:
On third-and-15 at his own 19-yard line, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix dropped back to pass and was immediately pressured, and he did about the worst thing he could have done: He dropped the football, which rolled into the end zone, where Pittsburgh’s T.J. Watt fell on it for a touchdown.

The player everyone is watching today is Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph, making his first start of the season after Pittsburgh benched and then cut Aaron Rodgers. Rudolph hasn’t done anything of note — he has just five passing yards through two Pittsburgh drives — but he hasn’t made any big mistakes either.

Nix made a very big mistake, Watt capitalized, and that’s the difference in the game so far.

sports.title: Kyler Murray off injury report, likely to be No. 2 QB vs. Falcons
sports.summary: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is officially off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
sports.body:
While he’s not going back to his starting role after Minnesota traded for Kirk Cousins, he probably going to be a snap away.

“Kyler got some good work in today. Took quite a bit of the reps this week, look-team wise, and feels pretty good ,” head coach Kevin O’Connell said in his Friday press conference. “We’ll assess him where he’s at, but [he’s] likely to be the backup. Carson [Wentz] would be the No. 3.”

In his first season with the Vikings, Murray has completed 65 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions this season in his six starts.

sports.title: Vikings rule out Jordan Addison, Christian Darrisaw, Isaiah Rodgers for Week 12
sports.summary: The Vikings will not have a few key players when they host the Falcons on Sunday.
sports.body:
Head coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters in his Friday press conference that receiver Jordan Addison (thumb), offensive tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder), and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers (thigh) are all out for Week 12.

O’Connell noted that the team is hoping Darrisaw will return for Week 13. Ryan Van Demark is expected to start at left tackle.

Safety Harrison Smith (thigh) is questionable for the contest.

Defensive lineman Jalen Redmond (ankle), receiver Tai Felton (hip), receiver Myles Price (knee/groin), and quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) are all off the injury report and are healthy to play.

sports.title: Bills Mafia co-founder disappointed fans missed Goo Goo Dolls halftime show
sports.summary: The Goo Goo Dolls halftime set at Highmark Stadium in the rain was not shown during the national broadcast.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk will not play Sunday vs. Cardinals
sports.summary: While receiver Brandon Aiyuk joined the Commanders earlier this week, but his debut with the team will have to wait.
sports.body:
Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed to reporters in his Friday press conference that Aiyuk will not be elevated for Sunday’s game against the Cardinals.

Aiyuk has only had a couple of practices with Washington, but he’s impressed Quinn with his work so far.

“I think it’s not surprising, but I think the catch radius and how strong his hands were,” Quinn said. “I knew that, but I hadn’t seen it for couple of years I suppose. But, his aggressive nature to go get the ball and pluck it. He can get in and out of breaks very quickly. So, those were two of the things that caught my eye yesterday and today.

“But it’s a good first impression for sure. He’s like everybody else, working hard and trying to learn it. New faces, new scheme, new people. He’s off to a good start.”

Aiyuk has not played since the 2024 season. His first opportunity to get on the playing field may come in Week 13 when the Commanders face the Titans on the road.

sports.summary: NFL veterans called out Aaron Rodgers after a public diatribe against the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach led to the quarterback's release.

sports.title: Commanders CB Amik Robertson to miss second straight game
sports.summary: The Commanders got a win over the Bengals without cornerback Amik Robertson and they'll try to do it again when they face the Cardinals on Sunday.
sports.body:
Robertson remained out of practice this week with an ankle injury and head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Friday that he will not travel with the team to Arizona. Quinn said the team does not have any long-term concerns about Robertson’s injury at this point.

Robertson has 53 tackles, a forced fumble and 10 passes defensed in nine games this season.

The Commanders will release a full injury report later in the day, but Robertson is the only player who has missed practice this week.

sports.title: Bears call Colston Loveland week-to-week with a knee injury
sports.summary: Bears tight end Colston Loveland went for tests on his injured knee after leaving Thursday's game in the first quarter and the team updated his condition on Friday.
sports.body:
The Bears say that Loveland is considered week-to-week as the team heads toward a Week 13 game against the Jaguars. They did not comment on the specific nature of Loveland’s injury.

There was also no mention of injured reserve, which is a positive given reports earlier in the day that indicated Loveland was going to go on the list.

Loveland has 41 catches for 397 yards and three touchdowns. With Cole Kmet on injured reserve, the healthy Bears tight ends are Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson.

sports.title: Overturning Rashee Rice fourth-quarter catch to incomplete was correct call
sports.summary: Of course a Buffalo Bills site would run this article with this headline, right? Really though, I wanted to get the bottom of the controversial call that went in the Bills’ favor on the Chiefs second-to-last possession in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s epic 13-10 walk-off win over Kansas City on Th
sports.body: Of course a Buffalo Bills site would run this article with this headline, right? Really though, I wanted to get the bottom of the controversial call that went in the Bills’ favor on the Chiefs second-to-last possession in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s epic 13-10 walk-off win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night. And I’ve reached a very definitive conclusion. The review was correct. Rashee Rice did not catch the football. We have to dismiss the “eye test” here, because NFL’s rulebook is the governing guide to the game. That distinction first has to be established. As convoluted as it may be to some, this is the official rule. It’s a catch if a player: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/catch-rule.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] My good bud Joe Goodberry — a wildly popular and insightful Bengals analyst and Niagara Falls native + resident — explained Friday on Twitter. Here’s the start of his thread, which featured a civil disagreement (yes, they’re possible!) between Joe and Sam Monson of the 33rd Team: [Media: https://twitter.com/JoeGoodberry/status/2126328590811697279?a=Mts4-WLSLMAXwJ951Pc&s=20] Instead of pasting each component of the lengthy back-and-forth between Goodberry and Monson, I’ll summarize the correct interpretation of the rule here. Rice satisfied (a) and (b) on this play. He secured control of the ball first before hitting the ground, then his elbow hit the ground while in control. But, scroll up to check (c) again. Rice did not “perform an act common to the game” — because he was simply falling to the turf, not a common act — therefore he must survive the ground. So, (a), (b), and (c) together were not fulfilled. Had they been, it would have been a catch. Case close. Precisely what occurred on the Rice play is clearly defined in section (2) of the rule. It specifies if (a) and (b) are satisfied, a player does not “survive the ground” if he hits the ground and loses control of the ball, there is no possession if the ball hits the ground before he regains control. That is exactly what happened on the play. Was it an egregious loss of control from Rice? [Media: https://twitter.com/oscolaidhe55/status/2126329351419359373?a=TtIZoWiYSK7VSyxJqic&s=20] No. But any degree of losing control counts if the ball hits the ground in the process. Which is why the NFL got this call right.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers got no support from the Thanksgiving broadcasts
sports.summary: The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him.
sports.body:
Across the board, the reaction from the NFL’s analysts and broadcasters was negative.

Former Steelers quarterback and Fox analyst Terry Bradshaw went off . Fox’s Michael Strahan agreed that Rodgers shouldn’t have gone public with his complaints — calling him a “narcissist” and a “rich jerk” and a “rich bad teammate.”

Fox’s Howie Long said that the moment “defines who [Rodgers] is.”

“He’s a guy that I think picked the wrong sport,” Long said. “He probably should have played tennis.”

Fox’s Rob Gronkowski said that, even if a contender loses its starting quarterback, there’s “too much smoke” to justify bringing Rodgers in.

The CBS pregame crew offered similar views . Nate Burleson said Rodgers “ didn’t handle this right .” Bill Cowher said he hates to see a Hall of Famer go out this way . With their 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, the Bills have matched the best 11-game start in franchise history. It was ugly. It was wet. It was cold. It was supposed to be an epic showdown between two NFL MVP quarterbacks. But in the end, it was a 57-yard field goal in the rain that sailed straight and true off the foot of Tyler Bass as the clock expired. It would be another 24 years before Buffalo got off to another 10-1 start. sports.summary: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. sports.body: For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. After all, if you’ve listened to enough of Allen’s postgame press conferences, you know there’s one statistic he cares about more than any other — wins. With Buffalo’s 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Allen has now won 98 regular-season games, tying Russell Wilson for the most wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons. Wilson, who entered the league in 2012, never had a losing season during his first nine years with the Seattle Seahawks. He won double-digit games in eight of those nine seasons, including a career-high 13 in 2013. Allen, on the other hand, won just five games as a rookie in 2018. A year later, the Bills were back in the playoffs, and they haven’t had a losing season since. In fact, Buffalo extended its franchise record to eight consecutive winning seasons just last week with a win over the Miami Dolphins. Allen moved past Patrick Mahomes (95) on this particular list two weeks ago when the Bills beat the New York Jets. Now, having picked up another win at Mahomes’ expense, Allen has caught Wilson, too. Allen completed just 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards while adding 43 yards on the ground. The real hero of the night was Tyler Bass who scored seven of the team’s 13 points – including the game winning field goal from 57 yards. But football is a team sport, and Allen’s contribution still counts. And the win is his to claim. The Bills will be in New England next week, where Allen will have his first opportunity to take sole possession of the NFL record. Allen still has six regular-season games left in his ninth season. That gives him some time to make life a little more difficult for the next quarterback chasing this record.

sports.body: The New York Jets are 3-8. According to the NFL Playoff Picture (via the NFL Media Group), the Jets currently have a 1% chance of making the playoffs. If they lose to the Miami Dolphins in Week 12, that’ll reduce their chances to less than 1%. However, if they beat the fish, their playoff chances will double to 2%. Are you saying there’s a chance? There’s a section of the fan base that would prefer to see the Jets lose to both improve their draft positioning and to lessen the chances of Aaron Glenn returning in 2027. The problem, according to some of those fans, is that there are too many winnable games down the stretch for the Jets. On paper, the Jets will be or could be facing at least three backup quarterbacks (Carson Beck or Josh Johnson, Kyle McCord, and Tommy DeVito). Also, depending on whether the Buffalo Bills have anything left to play for in Week 18, that could be a fourth backup QB. Instead of complaining, why don’t we take advantage? This opens up a favorable pathway to go on a winning streak. Now, how likely is that? Well, that’s a different conversation altogether. The Jets haven’t won back-to-back games all season. They haven’t really upset anyone, and they haven’t consistently beaten teams that folks assume they should be able to beat. Both of those things would be necessary to even have a hint of the postseason. The other thing helping the Jets’ potential path is that the bottom of the AFC is falling apart. Pittsburgh is crumbling; the Jets have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland; they play New England; and Baltimore has a backup in at QB. I’m not saying it’s likely; I’m not guaranteeing it’s going to happen; all I’m saying is there’s a chance, and maybe that’s what Jets fans should be rooting for. The Indianapolis Colts are self-destructing. The Jets control their first-round pick. That pick has a great chance to be a top-three selection. The Jets don’t need to tank; the Colts can tank for them. So… playoffs?! Maybe I’m food drunk from Thanksgiving, but I’m starting to see the light! --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: Late in the Buffalo Bills win over the Kansas City Chiefs, a turning point in the game was decided by replay. On third down inside two minutes, Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice over the middle of the field and Rice was popped by Bills safety Amani Hooker. As he fell to the ground, the ball moved. On the field it was ruled a catch. Because it was inside two minutes, the replay official had to call for a review and not Bills head coach Joe Brady. After replay, it was ruled an incomplete pass. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the play, saying he didn’t like the call. “Not one that I agreed with,” said Reid of the replay review. “This came from New York,” Reid said. “They called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. To me that was not clear and obvious.” The NBC broadcast spent a lot of time on it during the game and again in the postgame. Rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it was a catch and the Chiefs should have moved the chains. Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. Playing against the future Kansas City Chiefs, Don Maynard caught 10 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown, while Art Powell added 8 catches for 110 yards and a touchdown. November 28, 1985: Detroit Lions 31 New York Jets 20 Eric Hipple threw four touchdown passes, three to Leonard Thompson as the Lions jumped out to a 24-3 lead and never looked back. November 25, 2010: New York Jets 26 Cincinnati Bengals 10 In the third meeting between these teams in eleven months, the Jets erased a 10-7 halftime deficit. sports.body: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary.
